newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly firmer but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly firmer but off highs.

text.p: Swiss shares ended Friday up slightly but below highs after release of U.S. jobs data.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 7.6 points, or 0.17 percent, at 4,471.5 points. The index had traded as high as 4,510.2 points during the session.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gained 2.61 points, or 0.09 percent, to 2,836.53 points.
Volume was 1.72 billion Swiss francs for the day, which was considered average to slightly lower than normal.
Dealers said investors continued to worry about possible further increases in U.S interest rates after U.S. March employment figures showed an earnings gain.
Some were predicting further U.S. interest rate increases, which could also have a negative impact on European rates, after last month's Federal Reserve tightening.
"I would not be surprised if the Fed raised interest rates by another quarter percentage point at its May meeting," one Swiss trader said. Volatility was also expected to remain high.
But at the same time, some traders believed that latest pullback may be positive.
"We are in the middle of a healthy correction phase, but I do not think anything dramatic will happen," one said.

He believed institutional investors were more likely to hedge their positions than sell. He added that U.S. investors could also turn to European markets if U.S. shares are perceived as having lost some appeal after today's numbers.
Among individual shares, Novartis registereds led the actives list, falling two francs to 1,719.
Nestle, UBS and Clariant were among the day's gainers.

Nestle added 16 francs to 1,650. UBS bearers rose 20 francs, or 1.61 percent, to 1,259. Chemical firm Clariant, which said Friday that its 1996 group net increased by 29 percent jumped 11 francs to 694.

Swissair shares fell one franc to 1,229. After bourse close Swissair's holding company, SAirGroup, reported a 497 million franc group loss for 1996, due in part to a complete write-down of its 49.5 stake in Belgian carrier Sabena.
Industrial concern Alusuisse, watchmaker SMH and financials CS Group, SBC Swiss Re and Winterthur were among the losers.
